clue.text: Sultanate may burn that is upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and jumbling, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A warning that a ruler's realm might go up in flames, which would be distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' shuffles BURN with IE (from 'that is') to give the country; 'may' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich state on Borneo ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Flag a bold newspaper headline

explanation.surface: A banner and a big front-page splash, two ways of announcing news.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant is called this, and so is a headline running right across a newspaper page.

clue.text: Unapproved union action from slight tinkering

indicators.note: 'from' here means 'made out of', so the answer is built from these two words with their letters reworked

explanation.surface: A walkout without official backing sparked by a minor bit of meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of SLIGHT TINKERING are rearranged; 'from' says the answer is made out of them. 'tinkering' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the material.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden stoppage called by workers without warning or formal union approval is named after a bolt from the sky.

clue.text: Critiques concerning such opinions

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
views are opinions held on a matter

explanation.surface: Critical pieces dealing with particular kinds of opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' only links the two halves, pointing back to the critiques.
explanation.definitionFit: Critiques are published assessments of plays, books or films, the same as notices written by critics.

clue.text: Rooster calls for cooked cod, also do it in a hash

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so these words have their letters scrambled

explanation.surface: Instructions for a fish supper: mash cooked cod into a hash.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is COOKED COD ALSO DO, fifteen letters; 'in a hash' scrambles them and 'it' only joins. 'cooked' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The crowing of a cockerel at dawn is written as this phrase, here in the plural.

clue.text: A follower ones taken family to see bathing suit

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter following A is B

indicators.note: the two ones have taken in the family, holding it between them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, so ones are two I's
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A tourist's instructions for spotting swimwear at the seaside, read as a series of steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' puts KIN between the two I's (from 'ones'), giving IKINI after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit worn on the beach.

clue.text: Have a breather but must not stop working

definitions.text: Have a breather but must not stop working

parts.words: Have a breather but must not stop working
parts.note: a 'breather' is read literally as an organ that breathes, one that must keep going even while its owner rests

explanation.surface: Advice to take a rest while still keeping busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a breather' suggests a rest; read literally, a breather is a body part that breathes and can never take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the pair of breathing organs in the chest works nonstop to take in air.

clue.text: Worry about sea mist

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about fog rolling in off the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only links. A sea fret is a cold mist from the sea on Britain's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To be anxious and agitated is one sense; the other is a coastal fog drifting inland from the sea.

clue.text: Wrath of one again

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone's anger flaring up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger or fury.

clue.text: Detestable as half good promissory notes

indicators.note: only half of the word good is used, its second pair of letters

parts.note: IOUs ('I owe you') are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Grumbling that a pile of IOUs is only half as good as cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the back half of GOOD, giving OD; 'as' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful or repugnant.

clue.text: Entangle with open-ended net

indicators.note: 'open-ended' is read as the end of the word open, its closing pair of letters

parts.note: mesh is netting, a net of interlaced threads

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in a net that has no closed end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open-ended' is split: '-ended' takes the end of OPEN, giving EN; 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something in a mesh is to tangle it up, as in a fishing net.

clue.text: Slinking out with such suspicions

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of slinking are put out of order

explanation.surface: Creeping away under a cloud of suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SLINKING; 'with such' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Inklings are faint hints or vague notions that something is the case.

clue.text: Anniversaries of ice matches?

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
matches are marriages, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A question about celebrating frozen sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' is old criminal slang for diamonds and 'matches' are marriages, not games; 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: These celebrations mark sixty years of marriage, the jewel being the traditional gift.

clue.text: Set a broken leg

indicators.note: broken means the letters of leg are smashed and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A doctor putting a fractured limb in plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like setting a bone; it is the definition, as jelly sets. 'a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set firm, as a jelly does when it cools.

clue.text: Take priority over whilst away smelling

parts.note: out means away, as in 'out of the office'
rank means smelling foul

explanation.surface: Pulling rank on someone while off somewhere stinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whilst' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be superior in rank is to have precedence over another.

clue.text: Flower city capital of Eritrea

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, the capital at the head of the word Eritrea

explanation.surface: A blossom found in the capital of an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows: a river. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, and the Ure flows through North Yorkshire.

clue.text: Room with old bag

indicators.note: with is read as the room having the next word within it

parts.note: a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A spare room crammed with an old piece of luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' is the start of the wordplay, not the definition; the bag is at the end, and 'with' is read as one word holding the other inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travel bag with handles.

clue.text: Highly disputed action of "the few"

parts.note: 'the few' are the RAF pilots of the Battle of Britain, and 'highly disputed' is a fight up in the air

explanation.surface: A controversial campaign by a small elite group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Few' is Churchill's name for the RAF fighter pilots of the 1940 Battle of Britain; 'highly' means high in the sky, not very.
explanation.definitionFit: Close combat between fighter aircraft is the classic aerial battle of that summer.

clue.text: Shrewd costing out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of costing are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A sharp mind working out prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COSTING.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Greek for knowledge, it means knowing or clever, though usually used of the early Christian sect claiming secret wisdom.

clue.text: They may show the way back in a saloon

definitions.text: They may show the way back in a saloon

parts.words: They may show the way back in a saloon
parts.note: the saloon is a car, not a bar, and the way back is the direction it moves in reverse

explanation.surface: Bar staff pointing a customer back to their table.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is a British name for a sedan car; the white lamps at the rear come on when it goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: White rear lamps on a car switch on to light the road behind while it backs up.

clue.text: Snare foolish parent

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters of parent behave wildly and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A silly mother or father caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch or trick someone, as in a trap.

clue.text: Confused turning 21 may cut ahead

indicators.note: these words say the letters are muddled and turned about

parts.note: 21 points to the answer of 21 Down, the word meaning snare

explanation.surface: A muddled driver, taking a wrong turn, may barge ahead in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused turning' rearranges ENTRAP, the answer to 21. Read 'ahead' as 'a head': a trepan bores holes in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a surgical saw for cutting a disc out of the skull; as a verb it means to operate with one.

clue.text: Takes men on board in the mating game

definitions.text: Takes men on board in the mating game

parts.words: Takes men on board in the mating game
parts.note: the mating game is chess, where checkmate ends play, and the men are pieces taken off the board

explanation.surface: Someone welcoming new sailors aboard, or picking up partners on the dating scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The mating game' sounds like dating but means chess, where taking an opponent's pieces is the move named here.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, taking an opponent's piece off the board is the same move as seizing a prisoner.

clue.text: Am taking first dirty affair to original sinner

indicators.note: taking means the word am takes in the following letters, holding them inside
first means the opening letters of the words dirty and affair

explanation.surface: Admitting to the first sordid fling, like the first sinner of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes D and A from 'dirty affair'; 'taking' puts them inside AM. 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man ate the forbidden fruit, committing the first sin.

clue.text: Ideal for long shots when behind the wheel

explanation.surface: A golfing tip delivered while sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with a large head is used for long tee shots; the other sense is a motorist steering a car.

clue.text: Mother may question patterned table linen

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: Mum might enquire about the fancy tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible woven fabric with a pattern, often used for tablecloths and napkins.

clue.text: Iraq initially will bash artificial language

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word Iraq

parts.note: a bash is a party, and so is a do

explanation.surface: A news report that Iraq will at first strike out at a made-up tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a verb meaning hit; it is a noun, a party. 'will' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is a constructed international language derived from Esperanto.

clue.text: Pick up from being a little disheartened

indicators.note: being a little means only a small part of the word disheartened is used, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Lifting someone's spirits after a slight setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' only links; the answer sits in the middle of 'disheartened'.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sound with the ears, as in picking up a radio signal.
